<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<div id="p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent ltx_align_center">
<p id="p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Adaptive Time Series Reasoning via Segment Selection</span></p>
</div><span class="ltx_rule ltx_align_center" style="width:100%;height:1.0pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<div id="p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="p6.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Shvat Messica</span> <sup id="p6.1.2" class="ltx_sup">1 </sup> 
<span id="p6.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Jiawen Zhang</span> <sup id="p6.1.4" class="ltx_sup">2 </sup> 
<span id="p6.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Kevin Li</span> <sup id="p6.1.6" class="ltx_sup">3 </sup><sup id="p6.1.7" class="ltx_sup">1 </sup> 
<span id="p6.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theodoros Tsiligkaridis</span> <sup id="p6.1.9" class="ltx_sup">4 </sup> 
<span id="p6.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Marinka Zitnik</span> <sup id="p6.1.11" class="ltx_sup">1 </sup></p>
</div><span id="footnotex1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnotetext"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">footnotetext: </span><sup id="footnotex1.1" class="ltx_sup">1</sup>Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA
<sup id="footnotex1.2" class="ltx_sup">2</sup>The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
<sup id="footnotex1.3" class="ltx_sup">3</sup>Massachusetts Institute of Technology
<sup id="footnotex1.4" class="ltx_sup">4</sup>MIT Lincoln Laboratory. Correspondence to: Shvat Messica and Marinka Zitnik &lt;shvat.messica@fas.harvard.edu, marinka@hms.harvard.edu&gt;.
 
<br class="ltx_break"></span></span></span>
<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Time series reasoning tasks often start with a natural language question and require targeted analysis of a time series. Evidence may span the full series or appear in a few short intervals, so the model must decide what to inspect. Most existing approaches encode the entire time series into a fixed representation before inference, regardless of whether or not the entire sequence is relevant.
We introduce ARTIST, which formulates time-series reasoning as a sequential decision problem. ARTIST interleaves reasoning with adaptive temporal segment selection. It adopts a controller-reasoner architecture and uses reinforcement learning to train the controller role to select informative segments and the reasoner role to generate segment-conditioned reasoning traces and final answers. During inference, the model actively acquires task-relevant information instead of relying on a static summary of the full sequence. We use a novel hierarchical policy optimization approach for post-training that allows the model to excel in both segment selection and question-answering behavior.
We evaluate ARTIST on six time-series reasoning benchmarks and compare it with large language models, vision-language models, and prior time-series reasoning systems. ARTIST improves average accuracy by 6.46 absolute percentage points over the strongest baseline. The largest gains appear on rare event localization and multi-segment reasoning tasks. Supervised fine-tuning improves performance, and reinforcement learning provides additional gains by optimizing question-adaptive segment selection.
These results show that selective data use drives effective time-series reasoning.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18645v1/fig1_motivation.svg" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:606/173;" width="606" height="173"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span>
(a) Time-series reasoning: answering a natural language question given a time series. (b) ARTIST alternates between reasoning and adaptive segment selection, choosing the next segment based on the question and intermediate outputs, and stopping once it can produce the final answer.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Time-series modeling has long been shaped by tasks such as forecasting <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Das et al. (2024)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al. (2025a)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2025b)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al. (2025c)</a></cite>, classification <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025f)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025d)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tran et al. (2025)</a></cite>, and anomaly detection <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al. (2025)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cai et al. (2025)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al. (2025)</a></cite>. Increasingly, however, real-world use cases begin with a natural-language question rather than a predefined label or prediction horizon. A clinician may ask why a patient’s vital signs deteriorated after a medication change, and an analyst may ask what triggered a regime shift in a market indicator. Answering these questions requires linking the question to patterns in the time series and grounding the answer in relevant segments. This emerging setting, known as time series reasoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chow et al. (2024)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kong et al. (2025b)</a></cite>, asks models to answer natural language questions by identifying and analyzing the task-relevant parts of a time series.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Recent work has examined how to interface time series with large language models (LLMs). As in Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>a, approaches mainly differ in how they convert a time series into an LLM input, including textual serialization <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Alnegheimish et al. (2024)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Luo et al. (2025)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025e)</a></cite>, rendered plots <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025c)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. (2025a)</a></cite>, and learned embeddings <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al. (2024)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lei et al. (2025)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Langer et al. (2025)</a></cite>. These designs improve modality alignment but keep inference static: the model receives a fixed view of the full time series and must answer from that view. This is limiting for multi-step reasoning, where intermediate conclusions should change what the model inspects next. For example, a clinical deterioration query may first check for an abrupt spike, then shift to a different window or a narrower interval to test a hypothesis. More broadly, relevant temporal segments are query- and step-dependent. Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>b shows the desired behavior: reasoning interleaved with temporal segment selection, stopping when the model is ready to answer.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A key missing capability is question-adaptive information selection during inference. Time series inputs are long and temporally heterogeneous, and the same sequence can support many different questions that require different regions and different resolutions. As a result, forcing the model to process a fixed view of the full series can dilute salient local structure and, in long sequences, can degrade performance by mixing irrelevant context with task-relevant information. Related problems have been studied in text-vision reasoning, where models learn to search or zoom into regions conditioned on intermediate steps <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al. (2025a)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. (2025c)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al. (2025)</a></cite>. However, an analogous mechanism for time-series reasoning remains underexplored, despite the strong need for adaptive localization in long time series.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Two challenges make question-adaptive segment selection difficult in time series reasoning. First, unlike images, time series rarely include task-agnostic annotations that identify segments relevant to a given question. Relevant segments depend on the question, so the model must decide during inference which parts of time series to inspect.
Second, many post-training methods use reinforcement learning to optimize sequential decision making at the level of output tokens (e.g., PPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Schulman et al. (2017)</a></cite>, GRPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al. (2024b)</a></cite>, DAPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al. (2025a)</a></cite>). Token-level optimization becomes difficult when a task requires multiple sub-tasks and the reasoning horizon is long. Credit assignment then becomes diffuse: key steps such as tool calls or information selection occupy only a small part of the token sequence, so their effect on final output is hard to isolate and optimize. Approaches that disentangle traces into components and optimize them with role-specific objectives can target these steps directly <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Klissarov et al. (2025)</a></cite>. This motivates our present work on separating temporal segment acquisition from time series answer generation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Present work.</span>
ARTIST (Adaptive Reasoning for TIme-Series via Temporal Selection) is a time-series reasoning approach where an LLM is trained to treat time series as an active resource during inference (Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). It interleaves reasoning with temporal segment selection by training a single policy to operate in two roles. A high-level <em id="S1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">controller</em> selects the next segment and decides when to stop, conditioned on the question and intermediate outputs. A low-level <em id="S1.p5.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">reasoner</em> produces intermediate reasoning steps and the final answer conditioned on the selected segments. This separation explicitly decouples <em id="S1.p5.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">where to look</em> from <em id="S1.p5.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">how to reason</em>.
ARTIST is trained in two stages. First, we apply supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on curated traces that interleave segment selection with natural language reasoning. Second, we use collaborative self-play reinforcement learning to jointly optimize both roles. The controller is trained with a reliability-based reward that measures answer consistency under repeated sampling, and the reasoner is trained for correctness and format compliance conditioned on controller-selected segments.
Across six benchmarks in clinical, financial, environmental, and general domain time series reasoning, ARTIST outperforms large language models, vision-language models, and prior time-series reasoning systems. It achieves an average accuracy improvement of 6.46 percentage points over the strongest comparator, with gains of up to 12.5 points on datasets requiring localized or multi-segment reasoning. Supervised fine-tuning alone yields an average accuracy increase of 5.65 points over baselines, while reinforcement learning provides additional gains by optimizing question-adaptive segment selection. Further, ARTIST typically uses only 30-70% of the input time series sample per query, showing that selective temporal analysis improves accuracy without requiring full time series consumption.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Contributions.</span>
(1) We present adaptive segment selection for time series reasoning. The model iteratively chooses temporal segments to inspect and updates its reasoning based on the retrieved segments. This setting does not assume pre-defined segment labels.
(2) We introduce a hierarchical, collaborative self-play RL post-training method that separates segment selection from answer generation and trains each role with learning signals aligned to its role.
(3) On six benchmarks, ARTIST outperforms seven strong baselines. It improves average accuracy by 6.46 absolute percentage points over the strongest comparator while using a smaller fraction of the input time series.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Time Series Reasoning.</span>
Motivated by the need to solve real-world questions that require reasoning over evolving signals, as well as by advances in multimodal LLMs capable of processing non-textual inputs, recent studies have begun to formalize time-series reasoning. Several benchmarks have been introduced to evaluate such capabilities by pairing time-series signals with natural-language queries, including ECG-QA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oh et al. (2023)</a></cite>, TSQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kong et al. (2025a)</a></cite>, TRQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jing et al. (2025)</a></cite>, RCW <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025b)</a></cite>, and related datasets <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Merrill et al. (2024)</a></cite>. These resources frame temporal reasoning as question answering, explanation, or diagnostic inference over real or synthetic data, providing standardized settings for assessing LLM-based approaches.
In parallel with benchmark development, several modeling strategies have emerged to support time-series reasoning in LLMs. One line of work treats time-series values as textual inputs, allowing standard text-only LLMs to process temporal data without architectural modification. A second line couples a time-series encoder with a language model, such as ChatTS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al. (2024)</a></cite>, OpenTSLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Langer et al. (2025)</a></cite>, and ITFormer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lei et al. (2025)</a></cite>, mapping numerical observations into learned embeddings that the LLM can condition on for reasoning. A third line of work encodes time series into visual representations. VL-Time <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025c)</a></cite> and TimeMaster <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. (2025a)</a></cite> render signals as plots and use vision-language models to interpret them. These methods improve performance on time-series reasoning tasks, but they mainly address representation and modality integration, that is, how temporal signals are encoded and adapted for LLM processing. In contrast, the problem of selecting and analyzing temporal information during reasoning remains underexplored.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Self-Play RL for Reasoning.</span>
Self-play originated in game theory and reinforcement learning as a mechanism for learning in adversarial multi-agent settings, where agents improve by interacting with copies of themselves or past versions of their policies rather than with a fixed opponent, and where outcomes depend directly on the evolving strategies of other agents, requiring continual adaptation instead of optimization against a static objective  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. (2025b)</a></cite>.
More recently, this paradigm has been adapted to LLMs, where self-play is used to generate training signals and improve reasoning without relying on human-labeled data <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al. (2025)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fang et al. (2025)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025a)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2025c)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al. (2025)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al. (2025)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al. (2025b)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al. (2025b)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al. (2025b)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yue et al. (2026)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al. (2026)</a></cite>. In these studies, a single LLM assumes multiple roles within the same training loop, typically forming a difficulty-driven interaction. A <em id="S2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">proposer</em> generates tasks that challenge the model’s current capabilities, while a <em id="S2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">solver</em> attempts to solve them and is rewarded based on correctness. This alternation exploits the stateless nature of LLMs, allowing the same underlying model to perform distinct roles via prompting, thereby enabling data- and memory-efficient training without maintaining multiple separate models. As a result, self-play provides a mechanism for refining model behavior through role-based interaction and outcome evaluation, rather than reliance on external human annotations.
This is important for time-series reasoning and adaptive segment selection, where annotations specifying which temporal segments are relevant to a given question are difficult to obtain.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In contrast to adversarial self-play, ARTIST uses collaborative self-play to separate time-series reasoning into distinct roles. ARTIST assigns adaptive segment selection to a controller and answer construction to a reasoner. The controller selects temporal segments. The reasoner produces intermediate reasoning steps and the final answer conditioned on the selected segments. This separation distinguishes evidence acquisition from answer generation and supports role-specific learning signals.
Existing self-play methods, including AZR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al. (2025)</a></cite>, SPICE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025a)</a></cite>, and SPELL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2025c)</a></cite>, optimize each role with myopic objectives that reward the best immediate response within a single round. These objectives do not match temporal segment selection, where the model must build an informative set of segments across multiple rounds. ARTIST addresses this mismatch with hierarchical optimization. The controller receives trajectory-level supervision with credit assigned across interaction rounds, while the reasoner is optimized at the final round conditioned on the selected segments.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S2.F2" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<figure id="S2.F2.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18645v1/fig2a_generation.svg" id="S2.F2.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:673/130;" width="673" height="130"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(a) </span>Interaction Trajectory Rollout (Generation).</figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<figure id="S2.F2.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18645v1/fig2b_update.svg" id="S2.F2.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:673/86;" width="673" height="86"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(b) </span>Unified Policy Update (Optimization).</figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span><span id="S2.F2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Overview of ARTIST.</span>
(a) Given a question and a time series, a high-level controller iteratively selects informative temporal segments, while a low-level reasoner produces intermediate reasoning traces and answers conditioned on the accumulated segment set. The controller decides whether to continue selecting or accept it as a final answer and segment list.
(b) For each training example, multiple reasoning rollouts are generated per controller trajectory. Reasoner rewards are group-normalized across reasoning rollouts, while controller rewards are computed using the associated reasoning outcomes and normalized across controller trajectories. Both signals are used for a joint policy update.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>ARTIST</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Problem Setup and Notation</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We study <em id="S3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">time-series reasoning</em> for a natural-language question <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> paired with a time series
<math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times V}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> is the sequence length and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of variables.
A time-series large language model <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> generates a textual response <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}(q,T)\to Y." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}(q,T)\to Y.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">In this paper, we focus on the univariate setting (<math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V=1</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Time Series Reasoning.</span>
We view reasoning as searching for a high-probability inference path that links <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(q,T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(q,T)</annotation></semantics></math> to a correct answer.
Concretely, we introduce a latent sequence of intermediate steps <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z=(z_{1},\dots,z_{L})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=(z_{1},\dots,z_{L})</annotation></semantics></math> and write:</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\theta}(Y\mid q,T)\;=\;\sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}}p_{\theta}(Y\mid z,q)\,p_{\theta}(z\mid q,T)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.391em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒵</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\theta}(Y\mid q,T)\;=\;\sum_{z\in\mathcal{Z}}p_{\theta}(Y\mid z,q)\,p_{\theta}(z\mid q,T),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> specifies <em id="S3.SS1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">how</em> the model inspects and interprets the signal before producing <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Segments.</span>
A segment is a contiguous slice of the time series <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, denoted
<math id="S3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="s=T_{t_{\text{start}}:t_{\text{end}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>T</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mtext>start</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mtext>end</mtext></msub></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=T_{t_{\text{start}}:t_{\text{end}}}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\leq t_{\text{start}}&lt;t_{\text{end}}\leq H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mtext>start</mtext></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mtext>end</mtext></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\leq t_{\text{start}}&lt;t_{\text{end}}\leq H</annotation></semantics></math>.
We maintain an accumulated segment list <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}=[s^{1},\dots,s^{K}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}=[s^{1},\dots,s^{K}]</annotation></semantics></math> over multiple reasoning steps.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Controller-Reasoner Roles in ARTIST</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">ARTIST is a collaborative self-play model that equips a single policy model <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> with both <em id="S3.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">adaptive segment localization</em> and <em id="S3.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">segment-conditioned reasoning</em>.
The same underlying model is invoked in two roles via role-specific prompting, yielding <em id="S3.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">controller</em> <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}^{\text{ctl}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}^{\text{ctl}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <em id="S3.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">reasoner</em> <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}^{\text{rsn}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}^{\text{rsn}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The controller decides which temporal segments to inspect and when to terminate the interaction, while the reasoner generates a reasoning trace and a final answer conditioned on the accumulated segments.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Each training iteration consists of (i) generating rollouts through Controller-Reasoner interaction and (ii) computing a joint policy update. Figure <a href="#S2.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 2 Related Work" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> illustrates the rollout and update structure, and Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 3.5 Hierarchical Policy Optimization ‣ 3 ARTIST" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> summarizes the optimization process.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Interaction Trajectory Rollout</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a given question-time series pair <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(q,T)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(q,T)</annotation></semantics></math>, an <em id="S3.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">interaction trajectory</em> <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is a sequence of Controller-Reasoner interaction rounds indexed by <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1,2,\dots,L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1,2,\dots,L</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> is the realized number of rounds until termination.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Controller Step.</span>
At round <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, the Controller receives the current state:</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}^{\text{ctl}}=\bigl(q,T,\mathcal{S}_{i-1},a_{i-1},\hat{y}_{i-1}\bigr)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}^{\text{ctl}}=\bigl(q,T,\mathcal{S}_{i-1},a_{i-1},\hat{y}_{i-1}\bigr),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathcal{S}_{0},a_{0},\hat{y}_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathcal{S}_{0},a_{0},\hat{y}_{0})</annotation></semantics></math> are empty at initialization. In all subsequent interaction rounds <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i-1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{i-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{i-1}</annotation></semantics></math> are the reasoning trace and answer provided by the Reasoner in the previous round <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i-1</annotation></semantics></math>.
The controller then outputs a reasoning trace <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and a termination decision
<math id="S3.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}\in\{\textsc{Continue},\textsc{Accept}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Continue</mtext><mo>,</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Accept</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}\in\{\textsc{Continue},\textsc{Accept}\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
If <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}=\textsc{Continue}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Continue</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}=\textsc{Continue}</annotation></semantics></math>, it additionally proposes a new segment <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(u_{i},d_{i},s_{i})\sim\pi^{\text{ctl}}_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{i}^{\text{ctl}})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∼</mo><msubsup><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(u_{i},d_{i},s_{i})\sim\pi^{\text{ctl}}_{\theta}(\cdot\mid x_{i}^{\text{ctl}}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.3" class="ltx_p">and we append the new segment to the segment list <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{(i)}\leftarrow\mathcal{S}_{i-1}\cup\{s_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{(i)}\leftarrow\mathcal{S}_{i-1}\cup\{s_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
If <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}=\textsc{Accept}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Accept</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}=\textsc{Accept}</annotation></semantics></math>, the interaction terminates and the answer outputted by the Reasoner step in the previous round, <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{i-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{i-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, is accepted as the final answer.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reasoner Step.</span>
If <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}=\textsc{Continue}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Continue</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}=\textsc{Continue}</annotation></semantics></math>, the Reasoner is invoked with the updated segment list <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and produces a reasoning trace <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and answer <math id="S3.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(a_{i},\hat{y}_{i})\sim\pi^{\text{rsn}}_{\theta}(\cdot\mid q,\mathcal{S}_{i})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∼</mo><msubsup><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a_{i},\hat{y}_{i})\sim\pi^{\text{rsn}}_{\theta}(\cdot\mid q,\mathcal{S}_{i}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Formally, we define an interaction trajectory as:</p>
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=\bigl\{(u_{i},s_{i},d_{i},a_{i},\hat{y}_{i})\bigr\}_{i=1}^{L},\qquad d_{L}=\textsc{Accept}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Accept</mtext></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=\bigl\{(u_{i},s_{i},d_{i},a_{i},\hat{y}_{i})\bigr\}_{i=1}^{L},\qquad d_{L}=\textsc{Accept}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p4.2" class="ltx_p">We further define two sub-trajectories of an interaction trajectory: <em id="S3.SS3.p4.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">controller trajectory</em> as <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{ctl}}=\{(u_{i},s_{i},d_{i})\}_{i=1}^{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{ctl}}=\{(u_{i},s_{i},d_{i})\}_{i=1}^{L}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the <em id="S3.SS3.p4.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">reasoner trajectory @ round <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math></em> as <math id="S3.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{rsn, i}}=(a_{i},\hat{y}_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>rsn, i</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{rsn, i}}=(a_{i},\hat{y}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Reward Functions</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We define rewards for the two roles based on answer correctness, reliability across repeated trials, and format compliance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Correctness Reward.</span>
Given a question <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, gold answer <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, and prediction <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}</annotation></semantics></math>, we define the correctness reward as:</p>
<table id="S3.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E7.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="C(q,y^{*},\hat{y})=\mathbf{1}\!\left[\hat{y}=y^{*}\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.108em">=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C(q,y^{*},\hat{y})=\mathbf{1}\!\left[\hat{y}=y^{*}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reliability Reward.</span>
Given <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> and a segment list <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math>, we define reliability as the expected correctness of the Reasoner under repeated sampling conditioned on <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(q,\mathcal{S})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(q,\mathcal{S})</annotation></semantics></math>.
In practice, we estimate it with <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> independent rollouts <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{y}^{(n)}\sim\pi_{\theta}^{\text{rsn}}(\cdot\mid q,\mathcal{S}),n=1,\dots,N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>∼</mo><msubsup><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}^{(n)}\sim\pi_{\theta}^{\text{rsn}}(\cdot\mid q,\mathcal{S}),n=1,\dots,N</annotation></semantics></math> and then calculate:</p>
<table id="S3.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\begin{split}D(q,\mathcal{S},y^{*})=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mathbf{1}\!\left[\hat{y}^{(n)}=y^{*}\right]\\
=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}C(q,y^{*},\hat{y}^{(n)}).\end{split}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtable displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_right" columnalign="right"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mpadded style="width:0.886em;" width="0.886em"><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo></mpadded><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>N</mi></msup><mo>[</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>]</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_right" columnalign="right"><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{split}D(q,\mathcal{S},y^{*})=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mathbf{1}\!\left[\hat{y}^{(n)}=y^{*}\right]\\
=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}C(q,y^{*},\hat{y}^{(n)}).\end{split}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.3" class="ltx_p">A higher reliability reward indicates that the selected segments <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> make the Reasoner consistently produce the correct answer under sampling noise, and we use it as the learning signal for the Controller.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Controller Format Score.</span>
Each controller step receives a per-step format score <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> (see Appendix <a href="#A1.SS6" title="A.6 Format Reward ‣ Appendix A Controller and Reasoner Objectives and Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.6</span></a>).
Given controller trajectory <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{ctl}}=\{(u^{i},d^{i},s^{i})\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{ctl}}=\{(u^{i},d^{i},s^{i})\}</annotation></semantics></math>, and letting <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{I}_{\text{viol}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}})\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝕀</mi><mtext>viol</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{I}_{\text{viol}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}})\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> indicate whether <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{ctl}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{ctl}}</annotation></semantics></math> contains any critical violation, we define:</p>
<table id="S3.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E9.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="F_{\text{ctl}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}})=\bigl(1-\mathbb{I}_{\text{viol}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}})\bigr)\cdot\frac{1}{L}\sum_{i=1}^{L}f_{i}\;-\;\mathbb{I}_{\text{viol}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝕀</mi><mtext>viol</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.055em">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>L</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></munderover><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.502em">−</mo><msub><mi>𝕀</mi><mtext>viol</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\text{ctl}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}})=\bigl(1-\mathbb{I}_{\text{viol}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}})\bigr)\cdot\frac{1}{L}\sum_{i=1}^{L}f_{i}\;-\;\mathbb{I}_{\text{viol}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Controller Reward.</span>
The controller reward is defined as:</p>
<table id="S3.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\text{ctl}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}},D)=\begin{cases}-1&amp;\text{if }F_{\text{ctl}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}})&lt;0,\\[4.0pt]
w_{D}\,D+w_{f}\,F_{\text{ctl}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}})&amp;\text{otherwise},\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>if </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>otherwise</mtext><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\text{ctl}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}},D)=\begin{cases}-1&amp;\text{if }F_{\text{ctl}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}})&lt;0,\\[4.0pt]
w_{D}\,D+w_{f}\,F_{\text{ctl}}(\tau_{\text{ctl}})&amp;\text{otherwise},\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{D},w_{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{D},w_{f}</annotation></semantics></math> are tunable hyperparameters.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reasoner Reward.</span>
Given a final-round reasoner trajectory <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{rsn}}=(a,\hat{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{rsn}}=(a,\hat{y})</annotation></semantics></math> with correctness <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=C(q,y^{*},\hat{y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=C(q,y^{*},\hat{y})</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S3.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\text{rsn}}(\tau_{\text{rsn}},c)=w_{c}\,c+w_{e}\,F_{\text{rsn}}(\tau_{\text{rsn}})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\text{rsn}}(\tau_{\text{rsn}},c)=w_{c}\,c+w_{e}\,F_{\text{rsn}}(\tau_{\text{rsn}}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p4.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\text{rsn}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\text{rsn}}</annotation></semantics></math> scores format compliance (Appendix <a href="#A1.SS6" title="A.6 Format Reward ‣ Appendix A Controller and Reasoner Objectives and Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.6</span></a>) and <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{c},w_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>c</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{c},w_{e}</annotation></semantics></math> are tunable hyperparameters.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.5 </span>Hierarchical Policy Optimization</h3>

<div id="S3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Fig. <a href="#S2.F2.sf2" title="Figure 2(b) ‣ Figure 2 ‣ 2 Related Work" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2(b)</span></a>, we use nested rollouts to obtain separate learning signals for the Controller and Reasoner behavior, and combine them into a joint update. Decomposing the parameter update in this way enables more precise credit assignment, as advantage signals are propagated only to the relevant tokens for each role.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Nested Rollouts.</span>
For each training example <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(q,T,y^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(q,T,y^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>, we first sample <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> interaction trajectories
<math id="S3.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\tau^{(g)}\}_{g=1}^{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\tau^{(g)}\}_{g=1}^{G}</annotation></semantics></math> following Sec. <a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Interaction Trajectory Rollout ‣ 3 ARTIST" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>.
Let the terminating round of <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau^{(g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau^{(g)}</annotation></semantics></math> be <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{(g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{(g)}</annotation></semantics></math>, and let the final segment list be <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}^{(g)}_{L^{(g)}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}^{(g)}_{L^{(g)}}</annotation></semantics></math>
(<span id="S3.SS5.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_smallcaps">Accept</span> does not add a new segment).
For each interaction trajectory <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, we then resample the Reasoner <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> times conditioned on the same final segment list, and denote these final-round reasoner trajectories as
<math id="S3.SS5.p2.m10" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\tau_{\text{rsn},L^{(g)}}^{(g,n)}=(a_{L^{(g)}}^{(g,n)},\hat{y}_{L^{(g)}}^{(g,n)}),n=1,\dots,N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mtext>rsn</mtext><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{rsn},L^{(g)}}^{(g,n)}=(a_{L^{(g)}}^{(g,n)},\hat{y}_{L^{(g)}}^{(g,n)}),n=1,\dots,N</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We then compute the mean and variance correctness rewards for reasoner trajectories, i.e., <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mu}^{(g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>μ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mu}^{(g)}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\sigma}^{(g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\sigma}^{(g)}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\mu}^{(g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>μ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\mu}^{(g)}</annotation></semantics></math> equals the reliability reward in Eq. (<a href="#S3.E8" title="Equation 8 ‣ 3.4 Reward Functions ‣ 3 ARTIST" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>) for the final segments <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}^{(g)}_{L^{(g)}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}^{(g)}_{L^{(g)}}</annotation></semantics></math> produced in rollout <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Higher-Level Advantage Calculation for Controller.</span>
The Controller is optimized as a high-level policy that iteratively localizes segments across multiple interactions with the Reasoner and decides when the current information is sufficient.
For each interaction rollout <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\{1,\dots,G\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\{1,\dots,G\}</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute a Controller reward
<math id="S3.SS5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\text{ctl}}^{(g)}=R_{\text{ctl}}\!\bigl(\tau_{\text{ctl}}^{(g)},\,r_{\mu}^{(g)}\bigr)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>μ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\text{ctl}}^{(g)}=R_{\text{ctl}}\!\bigl(\tau_{\text{ctl}}^{(g)},\,r_{\mu}^{(g)}\bigr)</annotation></semantics></math> for controller trajectory <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{ctl}}^{(g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{ctl}}^{(g)}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We then form group-relative advantages
<math id="S3.SS5.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\hat{A}_{\text{ctl}}^{(g)}\}_{g=1}^{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mtext>ctl</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\hat{A}_{\text{ctl}}^{(g)}\}_{g=1}^{G}</annotation></semantics></math> according to Appendix <a href="#A1.SS1" title="A.1 Controller Advantages ‣ Appendix A Controller and Reasoner Objectives and Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lower-Level Advantage Calculation for Reasoner.</span>
The Reasoner is optimized as a low-level policy that maximizes answer quality and formatting conditioned on the segments selected by the Controller.
Unlike the Controller, the Reasoner update optimizes only the final-round rollouts under a fixed segment list, disentangling the optimization of Reasoner behavior from the variance in quality of the segments selected by the Controller.
For each interaction rollout <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, we draw <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> independent final-round Reasoner rollouts
