<math id="S3.SS5.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\tau_{\text{rsn},L^{(g)}}^{(g,n)}\}_{n=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mtext>rsn</mtext><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\tau_{\text{rsn},L^{(g)}}^{(g,n)}\}_{n=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> under the same <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Using all <math id="S3.SS5.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G\times N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G\times N</annotation></semantics></math> rollouts for every update can be memory-intensive, and many groups provide limited learning signal when their rewards are nearly identical. We therefore update the Reasoner using a single group <math id="S3.SS5.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> selected by <em id="S3.SS5.p6.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">variance-guided sampling</em>, which prioritizes interaction trajectory that induce diverse outcomes and thus yield a more informative within-group advantage signal:</p>
<table id="S3.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(g)\;\propto\;r_{\sigma}^{(g)}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">∝</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(g)\;\propto\;r_{\sigma}^{(g)},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p6.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS5.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\sigma}^{(g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\sigma}^{(g)}</annotation></semantics></math> is the variance of correctness across the <math id="S3.SS5.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> rollouts in group <math id="S3.SS5.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>. For the sampled group <math id="S3.SS5.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute a Reasoner reward for each trajectory
<math id="S3.SS5.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{rsn}}^{(g^{*},n)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{rsn}}^{(g^{*},n)}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E13.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="r_{\text{rsn}}^{(g*,n)}\;=\;R_{\text{rsn}}\!\Bigl(\tau_{\text{rsn},L^{(g)}}^{(g^{*},n)},\,C\bigl(q,y^{*},\hat{y}_{L^{(g)}}^{(g^{*},n)}\bigr)\Bigr)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0em">∗</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext></msub><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mtext>rsn</mtext><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>C</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\text{rsn}}^{(g*,n)}\;=\;R_{\text{rsn}}\!\Bigl(\tau_{\text{rsn},L^{(g)}}^{(g^{*},n)},\,C\bigl(q,y^{*},\hat{y}_{L^{(g)}}^{(g^{*},n)}\bigr)\Bigr),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p6.3" class="ltx_p">and form group-relative advantages <math id="S3.SS5.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\hat{A}_{\text{rsn}}^{(g^{*},n)}\}_{n=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mtext>rsn</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\hat{A}_{\text{rsn}}^{(g^{*},n)}\}_{n=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> according to Appendix <a href="#A1.SS3" title="A.3 Reasoner Advantages ‣ Appendix A Controller and Reasoner Objectives and Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS5.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Joint Update.</span>
Finally, we aggregate the Controller advantages <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\hat{A}_{\text{ctl}}^{(g)}\}_{g=1}^{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mtext>ctl</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\hat{A}_{\text{ctl}}^{(g)}\}_{g=1}^{G}</annotation></semantics></math> and the Reasoner advantages <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\hat{A}_{\text{rsn}}^{(g^{*},n)}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mtext>rsn</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\hat{A}_{\text{rsn}}^{(g^{*},n)}\}</annotation></semantics></math> into a joint update of the shared parameters <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> that maximizes the objectives in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Controller and Reasoner Objectives and Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>. Crucially, our Controller advantage signals are propagated across the Controller outputs from <em id="S3.SS5.p7.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">all</em> rounds <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{1,...,L^{(g)}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{1,...,L^{(g)}\}</annotation></semantics></math> in each interaction trajectory <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau^{(g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau^{(g)}</annotation></semantics></math>, optimizing the role’s behavior for incrementally choosing segments over multiple interactions that eventually result in the best segment <em id="S3.SS5.p7.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">set</em> long-term. In contrast, the Reasoner advantage signals are propagated only to the Reasoner outputs from the last round <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{(g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{(g)}</annotation></semantics></math> in each <math id="S3.SS5.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau^{(g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>τ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau^{(g)}</annotation></semantics></math>, optimizing the role’s behavior myopically to encourage focused, granular reasoning during question-answering. This hierarchical optimization setup is advantageous compared to previous self-play approaches for reasoning-based post-training that optimize both roles myopically, which would not be compatible for iterative segment selection.</p>
</div>
<figure id="alg1" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">

</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiments</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Datasets.</span>
We evaluate on six time-series reasoning benchmarks spanning diverse domains and question formats: TSQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kong et al. (2025a)</a></cite>, RCW <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025b)</a></cite>, ECG-QA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oh et al. (2023)</a></cite>, Sleep-QA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Langer et al. (2025)</a></cite>, TRQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jing et al. (2025)</a></cite>, and Etiological Reasoning (ETI) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Merrill et al. (2024)</a></cite>.
We follow each benchmark’s standard evaluation protocol, applying only minor restrictions for consistency (details in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>).
Dataset statistics are summarized in Table <a href="#A2.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ Appendix B Datasets" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Baselines.</span>
We compare against three families of models that support time-series reasoning.
(1) Text-based LLMs include GPT-5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Singh et al. (2025)</a></cite>, LLaMA-3-8B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Grattafiori and others (2024)</a></cite>, Qwen-3-8B and Qwen-3-14B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2025a)</a></cite>, which take serialized time series as input.
(2) Fine-tuned time-series reasoning models include ChatTS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al. (2024)</a></cite>, OpenTSLM-Flamingo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Langer et al. (2025)</a></cite>, and ITFormer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lei et al. (2025)</a></cite>, which pair a temporal encoder with an LLM backbone.
(3) Vision-based baselines include Qwen2.5-VL-3B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al. (2025)</a></cite>, VL-Time <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025c)</a></cite>, and TimeMaster <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. (2025a)</a></cite>, which operate on plotted time series. We use Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct as backbone for vision-based models.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Implementation &amp; Evaluation.</span>
We demonstrate the ARTIST approach using a Qwen3-4B backbone and a 5-layer MLP that encodes patch-based time-series inputs.
Segment selection is facilitated through a tool-calling mechanism that enables the model to iteratively retrieve temporal segments.
Training proceeds in two stages: (1) SFT, utilizing LoRA-based fine-tuning on structured reasoning traces that interleave natural language with segment-selection calls (Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C SFT CoT Data Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>); and (2) RL, employing full-parameter fine-tuning via our collaborative self-play algorithm.
Performance is measured using average Accuracy and F1 scores across 8 independent runs per dataset. For ARTIST, we maintain fixed temperatures for the reasoner (<math id="S4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7</annotation></semantics></math>) and controller (<math id="S4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math>). See Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E RL Training Configuration" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a> for comprehensive hyperparameter settings.</p>
</div>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison with general LLMs and time-series reasoning models.</span>
Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.1 Benchmarking Results ‣ 4 Experiments" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> shows that ARTIST achieves the best overall performance across all benchmarks.
Relative to the strongest baseline on each dataset and metric, ARTIST improves average accuracy by 6.46%.
RL further improves performance beyond SFT.
Compared with SFT, adding RL increases average accuracy from 63.61% to 69.26%.
<span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison with vision–language reasoning models.</span>
Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Study ‣ 4 Experiments" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> compares ARTIST with VLM baselines that operate on plotted time series.
ARTIST is best on five of six datasets (ETI, RCW, ECG-QA, TSQA, TRQA), while TimeMaster+RL performs substantially better on Sleep-QA.
We also observe that on ECG- and EEG-based datasets (ECG-QA and Sleep-QA), even VLMs without task-specific fine-tuning can be highly competitive, which may reflect stronger prior exposure to similar biomedical plots during pretraining.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Analysis of Time Series Data Utilization</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.1 Benchmarking Results ‣ 4 Experiments" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> examines how much of the time series ARTIST uses under RL and how this relates to accuracy on three datasets.
Across datasets, greater coverage does not consistently improve performance.
Instead, accuracy is highest when the model concentrates on a limited set of question-relevant segments, and it drops for questions that trigger near-complete sequence usage.
For Sleep-QA and TRQA, the best accuracy occurs when the model uses roughly 30–50% of the signal, whereas questions that induce 90–100% utilization are substantially less accurate.
TSQA exhibits a higher optimal range (about 70%), which is consistent with its shorter sequences and the need for proportionally broader coverage to capture relevant intervals.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Ablation Study</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct an ablation study to evaluate the core design choices of ARTIST, with results summarized in Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Study ‣ 4 Experiments" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Efficacy of Adaptive Segment Selection.</span>
Removing the controller entirely, which processes the full time series as a static input, leads to a significant performance drop of 9.30% in average accuracy. This confirms that processing the entire sequence can be suboptimal, as irrelevant temporal noise may obscure salient evidence. In contrast, ARTIST’s adaptive selection directs attention to task-relevant regions, enabling more precise reasoning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Joint Controller-Reasoner Optimization.</span>
<em id="S4.SS3.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Controller-only RL</em> configuration, where the reasoner remains frozen, results in an 8.94% decrease in average accuracy compared to the full model. This degradation arises from a distribution shift: during RL, the reasoner is conditioned on a dynamically selected set of segments chosen by the controller, whereas in SFT it was trained under a different input regime, receiving the full time series followed by a small number of additional segments. Freezing the reasoner therefore prevents it from adapting to the controller’s evolving selection policy. Jointly updating both roles mitigates this mismatch and maintains alignment between segment selection and downstream reasoning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reliability Reward.</span>
The most substantial performance decline (21.44% average drop) occurs when removing the <em id="S4.SS3.p4.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Reliability Reward</em>. Relying on single-rollout accuracy is insufficient due to the inherent stochasticity of LLMs: a reasoner may produce a correct answer by chance even when the selected segments are incomplete or irrelevant. In these cases, a single successful rollout can mislead the controller during learning. Our reliability metric uses nested rollouts to measure answer consistency across repeated samples. This estimate reflects whether the selected segment set reliably supports correct reasoning, rather than producing an isolated correct outcome.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Hierarchical Policy Optimization and Variance-Guided Sampling.</span>
Replacing the trajectory-level objective with a myopic objective leads to a 12.28% performance drop.
Here, the myopic objective refers to optimizing the controller based solely on the last interaction step, without propagating credit across the full interaction trajectory. With such an objective, the controller is encouraged to learn a greedy policy that is not optimized to make intermediate segment selections that lead to the best overarching segment set after multiple interactions.
In contrast, our hierarchical objective trains the controller to optimize a sequence of segment selections that, together, forms an informative segment set.
Replacing <em id="S4.SS3.p5.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Variance-guided Sampling</em> with standard stochastic sampling reduces average performance by 2.97%.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T2" class="ltx_table">

<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Illustration of Time Series Reasoning in ARTIST</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Study ‣ 4 Experiments" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> illustrates how ARTIST addresses queries by selecting a targeted set of informative segments.
In the apple sales case (Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Study ‣ 4 Experiments" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>,left), the controller first retrieves an early segment to establish a baseline level. Guided by the initial hypothesis of a potential trend shift, it then queries a late-sequence segment to test whether the change persists. The retrieved segment reveals a sustained level increase with higher variability, allowing the model to confirm a seasonal harvest uplift rather than a transient spike.
In the bird count example (Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Study ‣ 4 Experiments" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>,right), the model begins with a full-span segment to establish the sampling horizon and flag suspicious intervals. It then requests a higher-resolution segment around the anomaly to determine its duration and whether the signal recovers. This second segment shows a contiguous dip on the scale of months followed by a return to the prior level, which supports a temporary external influence rather than a persistent regime change.
Segment selection yields a verifiable evidence trail that ties the final answer to specific temporal segments.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">ARTIST is an RL approach that trains models to select task-relevant temporal segments while they reason toward an answer. Unlike prior methods that encode the full time series into a fixed representation, ARTIST interleaves segment selection with multi-step reasoning at inference time. On six benchmarks, ARTIST improves over strong LLMs, vision-language models, and time-series reasoning models.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Limitations.</span>
ARTIST incurs an additional inference cost due to iterative segment selection during reasoning. Furthermore, our evaluation focuses on univariate time-series tasks. Extending the framework to multivariate signals and irregular sampling remains an important direction for future work.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Impact Statement</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This paper presents work whose goal is to advance the field of machine learning. There are many potential societal consequences of our work, none of which we feel must be specifically highlighted here.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Controller and Reasoner Objectives and Rewards</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Controller Advantages</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We form group-relative advantages <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al. (2024a)</a></cite>
<math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\hat{A}_{\text{ctl}}^{(g)}\}_{g=1}^{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mtext>ctl</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>G</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\hat{A}_{\text{ctl}}^{(g)}\}_{g=1}^{G}</annotation></semantics></math> as:</p>

<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Controller Objective</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{o_{\text{ctl},i,t}^{(g)}\}_{t=1}^{T^{(g)}_{i}}" display="inline" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{o_{\text{ctl},i,t}^{(g)}\}_{t=1}^{T^{(g)}_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> be the sequence of the <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{(g)}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(u_{i}^{(g)},d_{i}^{(g)},s_{i}^{(g)})</annotation></semantics></math> at round <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> of interaction trajectory <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m5" For a batch of <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> questions, the Controller objective function is defined as</p>

<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We form group-relative advantages <math id="A1.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\hat{A}_{\text{rsn}}^{(g^{*},n)}\}_{n=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mtext>rsn</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\hat{A}_{\text{rsn}}^{(g^{*},n)}\}_{n=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> as:</p>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Reasoner Objective</h3>

<div id="A1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{o_{\text{rsn},t}^{(n)}\}_{t=1}^{T^{(n)}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>o</mi><mrow><mtext>rsn</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{o_{\text{rsn},t}^{(n)}\}_{t=1}^{T^{(n)}}</annotation></semantics></math> be the sequence of the <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{(n)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T^{(n)}</annotation></semantics></math> total tokens in the Reasoner output <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a^{(g^{*},n)}_{L^{(g^{*})}},\hat{y}^{(g^{*},n)}_{L^{(g^{*})}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a^{(g^{*},n)}_{L^{(g^{*})}},\hat{y}^{(g^{*},n)}_{L^{(g^{*})}})</annotation></semantics></math> at round <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{(g^{*})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{(g^{*})}</annotation></semantics></math> of Reasoner trajectory <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{\text{rsn}}^{(g^{*},n)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>τ</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{\text{rsn}}^{(g^{*},n)}</annotation></semantics></math>. For a batch of <math id="A1.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> questions, the Reasoner objective function is defined as</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<table id="A1.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E19.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{J}_{\text{rsn}}(\theta)=\frac{1}{B}\sum_{b=1}^{B}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\frac{1}{T^{(n)}}\sum_{t=1}^{T^{(n)}}\hat{A}_{\text{rsn}}^{(n)}\log\pi_{\theta}\Big(o_{\text{rsn},t}^{(n)}\mid q_{b},\{o_{\text{rsn},j}^{(n)}\}_{j=1}^{t-1}\Big)-D_{KL}(\pi_{\theta}||\pi_{\text{ref}})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒥</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>B</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>B</mi></munderover><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>N</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></munderover><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mtext>rsn</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mi>log</mi><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>o</mi><mrow><mtext>rsn</mtext><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext>ref</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{J}_{\text{rsn}}(\theta)=\frac{1}{B}\sum_{b=1}^{B}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\frac{1}{T^{(n)}}\sum_{t=1}^{T^{(n)}}\hat{A}_{\text{rsn}}^{(n)}\log\pi_{\theta}\Big(o_{\text{rsn},t}^{(n)}\mid q_{b},\{o_{\text{rsn},j}^{(n)}\}_{j=1}^{t-1}\Big)-D_{KL}(\pi_{\theta}||\pi_{\text{ref}})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">where the reference policy <math id="A1.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\text{ref}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mtext>ref</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\text{ref}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the reasoning model policy after SFT but before RL post-training.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.5 </span>Combined Objective</h3>

<div id="A1.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The two objectives above are aggregated into a joint objective, which is maximized via gradient ascent:</p>
<table id="A1.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{J}=\mathcal{J}_{\text{ctl}}+\mathcal{J}_{\text{rsn}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒥</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒥</mi><mtext>ctl</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒥</mi><mtext>rsn</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{J}=\mathcal{J}_{\text{ctl}}+\mathcal{J}_{\text{rsn}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.6 </span>Format Reward</h3>

<div id="A1.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce a format reward to ensure that both the Controller and the Reasoner produce
well-structured outputs that follow the required interaction protocol.
The format reward penalizes malformed, ambiguous, or incomplete responses and assigns
a hard failure to critical violations.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reasoner Format Reward.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given a reasoner completion <math id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute a scalar format score between -1 and 1.
The score starts from 1 and is reduced according to the following cases:</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reasoning block:</span> The completion must contain exactly one
<span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;think&gt;</span> block. Missing or multiple reasoning blocks incur a penalty.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Answer block:</span> The completion must contain exactly one non-empty
<span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;answer&gt;</span> block. Missing answers constitute a critical violation.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Separation:</span> The <span id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;answer&gt;</span> block must not appear inside
the <span id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;think&gt;</span> block; violations are penalized.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">If a critical violation occurs (for example, missing answer), the format score becomes negative,
triggering a hard failure.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Controller Format Reward.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let the controller produce a sequence of responses
where the final response must terminate the interaction.
Each controller iteration receives a per-step format score.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The trajectory level controller format score
is computed by averaging the per iteration scores, unless a critical violation occurs.
Specifically, the controller must satisfy the following rules:</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<ul id="A1.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Decision exclusivity:</span> Each step must contain exactly one decision:
either a segment selection or an acceptance.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Iteration structure:</span> All non-final steps must issue a valid segment selection call, while the final step must accepts the reasoner’s answer as final.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">segment selection validity:</span> segment selections must be valid JSON and specify a
time-series segment with valid bounds.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">If any step violates these constraints, a violation indicator
is triggered and the controller format score
is set to <math id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Hard Format Failure.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS6.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For both roles, any negative format score results in a hard penalty (-1).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>

<tr id="A2.T4.2.1.7.7.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T4.2.1.7.7.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:3.0pt;padding-right:3.0pt;">Sales/Energy/Entertainment/Tech/Transport/Health/Nature/Education</td></tr>
</table></td></tr>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We follow each benchmark’s standard evaluation protocol, with minor restrictions for consistency across datasets.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TSQA</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kong et al. (2025a)</a></cite> is a large-scale time-series question answering dataset composed of real and synthetic data, designed to evaluate models’ ability to understand and reason about temporal patterns beyond numeric prediction. We use its multiple-choice questions defined over univariate time series.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RCW</span> is a univariate acoustic time-series dataset within the TimerBed benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025b)</a></cite> that evaluates simple deterministic reasoning by requiring models to infer the presence of a North Atlantic right whale call from temporal–spectral structure in the signal.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">ECG-QA</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oh et al. (2023)</a></cite> is a clinical time-series question answering dataset designed to evaluate medical reasoning over ECG signals, consisting of 10-second 12-lead ECG recordings paired with clinical context. In this work, we only use binary (true/false) questions involving a single lead, requiring models to reason over univariate cardiac time series.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Sleep-QA</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Langer et al. (2025)</a></cite> is a clinical time-series question answering dataset designed to evaluate reasoning over sleep-stage dynamics, consisting of 30-second single-channel electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings annotated with sleep stages. Following prior work<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pouliou et al. (2025)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Langer et al. (2025)</a></cite>, non-REM stages 3 and 4 are merged, yielding five classes: Wake, REM, Non-REM1, Non-REM2, and Non-REM3.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TRQA</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jing et al. (2025)</a></cite> is a large-scale time-series reasoning benchmark; we use its characterization task, which evaluates reasoning about intrinsic properties of univariate time series through true/false and multiple-choice questions.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Etiological Reasoning (ETI)</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Merrill et al. (2024)</a></cite> is a time-series reasoning dataset that evaluates causal interpretation by requiring models to identify the most plausible generative scenario for a given univariate time series via multiple-choice questions. The original dataset consists of 6,978 synthetic time series; to obtain sufficient data for both RL and SFT, we additionally use a subset of the single–time-series (1TS) dataset released by the authors and adapt it to the etiological reasoning format using their provided code.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>SFT CoT Data Creation</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Supervised fine-tuning reasoning traces follow a structured, interleaved format that alternates between natural-language reasoning and explicit time-series segment selection. Each trace consists of multiple reasoning steps, where intermediate reasoning motivates the selection of informative temporal segments, followed by a final answer.
To construct these traces, we prompted GPT-5 to answer time-series questions conditioned on rendered visualizations. The resulting responses were then transformed into structured reasoning traces with explicit segment-selection steps and post-processed to ensure correctness, structural consistency, and adherence to the template.
A simplified example is shown in Figure <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C SFT CoT Data Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>. Figure <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C SFT CoT Data Creation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a> presents the prompt used to generate the raw responses from which the structured reasoning traces were derived.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.2" class="ltx_block">

<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">- The correct answer.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.8" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.8.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.9" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Your task has two parts:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.10" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.10.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.11" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.11.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.11.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.11.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.11.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p11.1" class="ltx_p">(1) Identify the specific contiguous segments of the time series that are essential for solving the question.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.12" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.12.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.12.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p12" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p12.1" class="ltx_p">- You may choose at most 3 segments.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.13" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.13.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p13" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p13.1" class="ltx_p">- Each segment must be at least 8 time steps long (inclusive).</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.14" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.14.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.14.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p14" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p14.1" class="ltx_p">- Segment boundaries must lie within [0, {ts_len - 1}].</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.15" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.15.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.15.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.15.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.15.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.15.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p15" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p15.1" class="ltx_p">- Only include segments that are strictly necessary. If the entire series is needed, use a single segment [0, {ts_len - 1}].</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.16" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.16.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.16.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.17" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.17.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.17.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.17.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.17.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.17.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p17" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p17.1" class="ltx_p">(2) Using only the identified segments and the metadata, provide a concise, step-by-step explanation that leads to the correct answer.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.18" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.18.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.18.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.19" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.19.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.19.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p19" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p19.1" class="ltx_p">Critical explanation constraint:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.20" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.20.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.20.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p20" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p20.1" class="ltx_p">- For each segment, you MUST separate:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.21" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.21.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.21.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p21" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p21.1" class="ltx_p">(a) The reasoning objective for selecting the segment, and</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.22" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.22.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.22.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p22" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p22.1" class="ltx_p">(b) The analysis of what the segment reveals.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.23" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.23.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.23.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.23.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.23.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.23.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p23" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p23.1" class="ltx_p">- The sentence explaining why a segment is chosen MUST NOT describe, summarize, or analyze the values, patterns, trends, or variability within that segment, but explain the rationale and how to approach the question correctly.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.24" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.24.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.24.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.24.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.24.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.24.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p24" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p24.1" class="ltx_p">- All observations and analyses of the segment MUST appear only in the subsequent sentence.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.25" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.25.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.25.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.26" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.26.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.26.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">

<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p26.1" class="ltx_p">Important constraints:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.27" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.27.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.27.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.27.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.27.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.27.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p27" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p27.1" class="ltx_p">- Base all explanations strictly on the observable behavior and statistical properties of the time series.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.28" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.28.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.28.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.28.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.28.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.28.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p28" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p28.1" class="ltx_p">- Do NOT use external context, prior knowledge of labels, or textual descriptions of answer options.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.29" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.29.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.29.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.29.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.29.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.29.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p29" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p29.1" class="ltx_p">- Do NOT mention or allude to any answer option or class label until the final answer line.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.30" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.30.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.30.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.31" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.31.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.31.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.31.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.31.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.31.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p31" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p31.1" class="ltx_p">Your response MUST follow exactly the structure below, with no additional sections or deviations:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.32" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.32.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.32.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.33" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.33.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.33.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p33" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p33.1" class="ltx_p">Important segments:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.34" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.34.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.34.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p34" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p34.1" class="ltx_p">Segment 1: [x1, y1]</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.35" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.35.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.35.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p35" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p35.1" class="ltx_p">Explanation:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.36" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.36.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.36.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p36" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p36.1" class="ltx_p">First, to solve the question, I need to &lt;state the reasoning objective&gt;.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.37" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.37.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.37.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.37.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.37.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A3.p3.pic1.1.37.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A3.p3.pic1.p37" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">

</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Supervised Fine-Tuning Configuration</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Prior to reinforcement learning, we train ARTIST through large-scale pretraining following the procedure described in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al. (2024)</a></cite>, enabling joint modeling of time-series representations and natural language inputs.
For each benchmark, we then independently perform supervised fine-tuning using LoRA adapters (rank 8, <math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=16</annotation></semantics></math>) for up to 5 epochs, with early stopping based on validation performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>RL Training Configuration</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We train ARTIST using fully on-policy reinforcement learning with full-parameter fine-tuning. Optimization is performed using AdamW with learning rate <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\times 10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\times 10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>. Each update processes a batch of 64 question and time-series pairs. For each pair, <math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G=6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G=6</annotation></semantics></math> interaction trajectories are sampled for the controller, and for each trajectory, <math id="A5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=6</annotation></semantics></math> final-round reasoner rollouts are generated.
During rollout generation, we use a controller temperature of <math id="A5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math>, a reasoner temperature of <math id="A5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7</annotation></semantics></math>, and top-<math id="A5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> sampling with <math id="A5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.95</annotation></semantics></math>. We apply KL regularization only to the reasoner objective with a fixed coefficient <math id="A5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=0.002" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.002</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=0.002</annotation></semantics></math>, using the SFT-initialized model as the reference policy <math id="A5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ref</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Training runs for one epoch over the dataset, and experiments are conducted on four NVIDIA H100 GPUs.</p>
</div>
</section>

<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">You are a time series expert. Analyze ONLY the given time series data and answer the question.</span>

<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.2" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;"></span></span></span>

<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"># Output Schema</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.4" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.4.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">&lt;think&gt;One-two sentences describing your reasoning and how you came to the answer.&lt;/think&gt;</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.5" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">

<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.6" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">

<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.7" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.7.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">

</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.8" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.8.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.9" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p9.1" class="ltx_p"># Rules (MANDATORY)</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.10" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.10.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">- No text outside &lt;think&gt; and &lt;answer&gt;.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.11" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.11.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.11.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.11.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.11.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p11.1" class="ltx_p">- In &lt;think&gt;, explain you reasoning, how you came to the answer, and reference segments by number (e.g., "Seg 2 rises ~0.3 at t=150-200").</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.12" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.12.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.12.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.12.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.12.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:21.0pt;"> </span><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.12.1.4" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:437.4pt;">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p12" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p12.1" class="ltx_p">- if evidence is insufficient, state the most likely answer and reflect uncertainty (consicely. i.e I’m not sure about the answer because...).</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.13" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.13.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p13" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p13.1" class="ltx_p">- In &lt;answer&gt;:</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.14" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.14.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.14.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p14" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p14.1" class="ltx_p">- first line is exactly A, B, C, or D.</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.15" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.15.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.15.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;"></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.16" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.16.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.16.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p16" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.p16.1" class="ltx_p"># Time Series Segments</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.17" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.17.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.17.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">

</span></span></span></span>
<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.18" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.18.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.18.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;"></span></span></span>

<span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.20" class="ltx_p" style="width:458.4pt;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.20.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:458.4pt;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span id="A6.p2.pic1.1.20.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:458.4pt;">
